title: [C12T4] - Understanding geothermal power generation
prompt: The diagram below shows how geothermal energy is used to produce electricity. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The diagram illustrates the process by which geothermal energy is utilized to generate electricity in a geothermal power plant, demonstrating the transformation of cold water into electrical energy through underground thermal resources.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, this is a linear process that harnesses the Earth's natural heat from hot rocks located deep underground to produce clean electricity. The system involves five distinct stages, from water injection to electricity generation, utilizing both underground thermal zones and surface-level mechanical equipment.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: The process begins with cold water being pumped down through an injection well to a depth of 4.5 kilometers below ground level, where it reaches the geothermal zone containing heated rocks. As the cold water comes into direct contact with these hot geological formations, it absorbs substantial thermal energy and transforms into hot water due to the intense underground temperatures. This heated water is then extracted back to the surface through a separate production well, bringing the absorbed geothermal energy to the surface level.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Once above ground, the hot water is converted into steam, which then goes into a turbine where the steam's pressure and heat cause the turbine blades to rotate. This mechanical energy from the spinning turbine powers a generator, which converts the rotational motion into electricity. The generated electricity is subsequently transmitted through power lines for distribution to consumers.
